walkthroughs.body_html:
Practical Skills in Biology — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Practical Skills in Biology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Practical Skills in Biology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: During an action potential, do Na+ and K+ move through the same channels?
options: Only Na+ moves during an action potential; K+ stays still.
No — voltage-gated Na+ channels open first (depolarisation, Na+ in), then voltage-gated K+ channels open (repolarisation, K+ out).
Na+ and K+ swap places through the same channel at the same time.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of the refractory period after an action potential?
options: Only Na+ moves during an action potential; K+ stays still.
The refractory period blocks all signals from reaching the neurone.
The refractory period exists because the cell runs out of energy and needs a rest.
It ensures action potentials travel in one direction only and limits the maximum firing frequency.
